item.description: Originally published in the January-February 2026 edition of the American Quarter Horse Journal. Republished in the True Dakotan with permission from the publisher.

item.title: Dean Honored With Lifetime Achievement Award for Service to Rural Medicine
item.description: After decades of caring for patients in Wessington Springs and advocating for rural health across the country, longtime family physician Dr. Tom Dean has received one of the profession’s highest honors.

item.title: Daylight Saving Time Begins Sunday
item.description: Daylight Saving Time begins on Sunday, March 8, 2026 at 2 a.m. On Saturday night, clocks are set forward one hour (i.e., losing one hour) to “spring forward.” Daylight Saving Time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026, at 2 a.m.

item.title: Cutler, Larson Inducted Into WSHS Athletic Hall of Fame
item.description: Two standout Spartan athletes were inducted into the Wessington Springs High School Athletic Hall of Fame Friday night during the boys basketball game against Sanborn Central/ Woonsocket. Richard Cutler and Sarah (Horsley) Larson were honored during halftime as the newest members of the Hall of Fame.

item.title: Spartans Cap Strong Season After Tight Regional Semifinal
item.description: A matchup between two of the state’s top Class B teams is typically reserved for the Barnett Center. Instead, the No. 1 Castlewood Warriors and No. 5 Wessington Springs Spartans met Saturday in the Region 2B semifinals at Huron Arena with a SoDak 16 berth on the line.

item.title: Operation Round-Up Grant Applications Due May 1
item.description: Central Electric Cooperative is accepting Operation Round-Up grant applications from local organizations until May 1. Through Operation Round-Up, groups can request up to $3,000 for projects that benefit cooperative members and their communities.

item.title: Preschool Open House, Enrollment Scheduled March 25
item.description: Families with young children are invited to attend the Wessington Springs Preschool Open House and Enrollment event later this month. The event will be held Wednesday, March 25, from 4 to 6 p.m.

item.title: Springs Area Bus Sees Strong Community Support
item.description: The Springs Area Bus meal service and Sunday service rides continue to operate thanks to strong community support in recent months. After being told by ROCS last year that approximately $1,500 in local monthly support would be needed to sustain those services, area residents have stepped up with donations totaling $5,988 from November 2025 through the end of February 2026.

item.title: Homegrown at School
item.description: New greenhouse, local donations and hands-on learning are transforming how students understand food Fresh watermelon and Wolsey-raised beef are showing up on lunch trays in the Wolsey-Wessington School District. Now, with a newly awarded $15,000 grant from Farm Credit Services of America, the district is preparing to take its growing farm-to-table program even further with the addition of a student-built greenhouse.

item.title: Pony Hills Sends Six to State, Shows Growth Across Program
item.description: Six area wrestlers will represent Pony Hills Youth Wrestling at the state tournament, capping off a season marked by growth and improvement across the program. State qualifiers include Mary Tanke, Kaddilac Coleman, Kix Coleman, Brecken Jensen, Hayes Cashman and McCrae Nickels.
